how_to_read: Each finding is a SUSPICION with its method attached, not a verdict. `severity` is how much it would matter if real; `confidence` is how likely it is to be real - they are different questions. Look up `check` in `checks` for the reasoning the check used and the false positives it is known to produce, and judge the finding against that rather than taking it on trust. `id` is stable across edits that only move the code, so it can be used to track or suppress a finding.
not_examined: Anything that requires running the program: rendering, timing, memory, and whether a button does what it says.
C++ template instantiation, overload resolution and macro expansion - names introduced by a macro body are not resolved.
Conditional compilation: both arms of an #ifdef are parsed, and checks that depend on control flow are suppressed across them.
Rust sources under native/ and the FFI boundary.
Generated build output, vendored headers and native/target/.

assert_with_work.title: An assertion that does the work
assert_with_work.why_it_matters: Q_ASSERT and assert compile out of release builds. An assertion whose expression has an effect behaves one way in a debug build and another in the build the user runs - the hardest class of bug to reproduce.
assert_with_work.method: A call to Q_ASSERT / Q_ASSERT_X / assert whose argument contains an assignment, an increment, or a call that is not a known pure accessor.
assert_with_work.known_false_positives: Calls that are pure but not in this module's list of pure names.

catalogue_counts_disagree.title: A catalogue summary number that the catalogue's own entries contradict
catalogue_counts_disagree.why_it_matters: The graph library and the Graph packs menu show these numbers. When they disagree with the entries they claim to summarise, the program states a figure that is simply false - and nothing on screen looks wrong, so it survives until somebody adds up the packs by hand. It had already happened: packs[].entryCount summed to 2116 against an entry_count of 2122, because one script recomputed the headline and another recomputed the packs and nothing compared them.
catalogue_counts_disagree.method: Recomputes entry_count, engine_count, category_count and every pack's entryCount from config/graph_catalogue.json's own entries, and reports any that differs from the value stored beside them.
catalogue_counts_disagree.known_false_positives: None. The entries are the catalogue; a summary of them has exactly one correct value.

catalogue_unverified.title: A graph the catalogue offers that nothing measures
catalogue_unverified.why_it_matters: An engine offered in the picker with no measured check behind it can render a blank figure and nobody finds out until a user picks it.
catalogue_unverified.method: Entries in config/graph_catalogue.json whose `verified` flag is false, and entries carrying no flag at all.

citation_styles_stale.title: The picker's style list is not the formatter's style list
citation_styles_stale.why_it_matters: The interface offers citation styles from a generated file and the science service formats from the Python table it is generated from. When they diverge, a style can be offered and then not applied - which is precisely the fault this area was rebuilt for: a `style` argument the formatter accepted and ignored, so a person who chose IEEE got APA with nothing on screen to say their choice had done nothing.
citation_styles_stale.method: Runs tools/make_citation_styles.py --check, which regenerates the list from graphvis_science/citation_styles.py and compares it byte for byte with config/citation_styles.json.
citation_styles_stale.known_false_positives: None. It is the same script that writes the file.

connect_without_context.title: A connect to a lambda with no context object
connect_without_context.why_it_matters: A three-argument connect with a lambda has no receiver, so the connection outlives the objects the lambda captured. It fires after they are destroyed.
connect_without_context.method: Calls named `connect` whose last argument begins with a lambda introducer and which have exactly three arguments.
connect_without_context.known_false_positives: A lambda that captures nothing with a lifetime shorter than the sender.

copy_per_iteration.title: A range-for that copies each element
copy_per_iteration.why_it_matters: `for (auto x : c)` copies every element. For anything larger than a pointer that is a per-iteration cost with no benefit, and the fix is one character.
copy_per_iteration.method: A range-for declaring a non-reference loop variable that the body never assigns to, where the body uses the variable as an object (member access or passing it on) rather than as a number.
copy_per_iteration.known_false_positives: Element types that really are cheap to copy but are not spelled as primitives.

dead_function.title: A function nothing calls
dead_function.why_it_matters: Code nobody runs is code nobody is testing, and it still has to be read and maintained.
dead_function.method: A function whose name appears exactly once across all C++ sources (its own definition) and never in any QML file, and which is not a Qt slot, signal, invokable, override, constructor, destructor, operator or main.
dead_function.known_false_positives: Anything called through a macro, a template this does not instantiate, or the Rust FFI boundary. Virtual overrides are excluded by looking at every declaration of the name, because `override` is written on the header declaration and not on the definition.

declaration_without_definition.title: A declared function with no definition anywhere
declaration_without_definition.why_it_matters: It links only because nothing calls it. The first caller is a link error.
declaration_without_definition.method: Delegated to tools/check_definitions.py, so that there is one definition of this rule rather than two that can disagree.
declaration_without_definition.known_false_positives: Whatever that tool's own limits are.

designed_colourmaps_stale.title: The designed colour-vision palettes are not what the designer produces
designed_colourmaps_stale.why_it_matters: ColourMapsCvd.h holds palettes built for a named colour-vision deficiency, and the separation each one achieves is written into the file as a comment and into its registry row as a number. A file edited by hand, or left behind when the designer changed, states a measurement nobody took - and that number is what the picker orders the colourblind category by.
designed_colourmaps_stale.method: Runs tools/design_cvd_colourmaps.py --check, which rebuilds every palette and compares the header byte for byte.
designed_colourmaps_stale.known_false_positives: None. It is the same script that writes the file.

disabled_block.title: Code inside #if 0
disabled_block.why_it_matters: Code that cannot compile is code nobody is maintaining. It reads as if it works.

duplicate_condition.title: A condition repeated in one else-if chain
duplicate_condition.why_it_matters: The second arm can never run: the first one with the same condition always wins.
duplicate_condition.method: Textually identical conditions at two positions of a single if/else-if chain.
duplicate_condition.known_false_positives: Conditions that read the same but depend on state changed by an earlier arm - possible, but then the chain is hard to read anyway.

engine_without_catalogue_entry.title: An engine the backend can draw and the catalogue does not offer
engine_without_catalogue_entry.why_it_matters: Work that shipped and cannot be reached. The code is there, tested or not, and no user can select it.
engine_without_catalogue_entry.method: String literals compared against a variable named `engine` inside the prepareEngineGroup dispatchers, checked against the engine names in config/graph_catalogue.json. The `engine ==` shape is required, not just the literal: without it the check matched axis labels and reported twenty engines that were never engines.
engine_without_catalogue_entry.known_false_positives: Engines deliberately reachable only as a variant of another.

expensive_call_in_loop_condition.title: A call re-evaluated on every iteration of a loop
expensive_call_in_loop_condition.why_it_matters: A loop condition runs once per iteration. A cheap accessor there is free; anything else is the loop body's cost multiplied by its length.
expensive_call_in_loop_condition.method: A call in a `for` or `while` condition whose name is not a known cheap accessor or literal constructor, where NOTHING it depends on changes per iteration: not its receiver, not its arguments, not the loop variable, and not anything the increment or body writes.
expensive_call_in_loop_condition.known_false_positives: Calls that are cheap but not in this module's list. Deliberately excluded: calls whose answer changes on its own - a timer's elapsed(), a stream's bytesAvailable() - because hoisting those does not speed the loop up, it stops it terminating.

filename_in_logic.title: A guard that names a source file
filename_in_logic.why_it_matters: A condition that compares against a source file's name goes stale the first time that file is split or renamed, and goes stale silently: the comparison simply stops matching and the guarded behaviour quietly stops happening. This project has hit it - a guard naming a file that had since been divided into six.
filename_in_logic.method: String literals ending in a source extension that appear as an operand of a comparison or a contains/startsWith/endsWith call.
filename_in_logic.known_false_positives: Diagnostics, log messages and error text that legitimately name a file.

frozen_list_rule.title: A hard-coded list used as a rule
frozen_list_rule.why_it_matters: A list of names written into a function is a rule frozen at the moment somebody typed it. It is right for the cases that existed that day and silently wrong for every case added afterwards, and nothing fails when it goes stale. This project shipped exactly this bug: a windowing rule correct for one class of engine was applied to all 434, and the fix was to ASK the engine rather than consult a list.
frozen_list_rule.method: A function body containing a literal container of four or more string literals, where the same function then performs a membership test (contains / indexOf / find / any comparison chain) against it.
frozen_list_rule.known_false_positives: Genuine fixed vocabularies - file extensions, units, an enum's spelling - are legitimately lists and will be reported here.

guard_after_use.title: A guard runs after the work it exists to prevent
guard_after_use.why_it_matters: A check placed below the first use of the thing it checks cannot prevent anything: by the time it runs, the dereference or the index has already happened. This is the most frequent root cause in this project's own history, and it is invisible to text search because a correct guard and a useless one are written identically - only their position differs.
guard_after_use.method: For each early-exit `if` whose condition is a pure NULL test on one pointer, look for an earlier dereference of that same pointer - `p->x` or `*p`. The declaration and its own initialiser do not count.
guard_after_use.known_false_positives:
A name reused for two unrelated pointers in one function.
Deliberately NOT reported: `container.append(x)` before `if (container.isEmpty())`. Building a list and then checking whether it came out empty is the normal idiom, not a guard in the wrong place - treating it as one produced 110 findings here, none of them real.

help_out_of_date.title: The shipped manual does not match its sources
help_out_of_date.why_it_matters: config/help_topics.json is generated from config/help_written.json and the program's own tables. If it has not been regenerated, the manual in the executable describes a version of the program that no longer exists - and it is the one document nobody can check against the thing it describes.
help_out_of_date.method: Runs tools/make_help.py --check, which rebuilds the document in memory and compares it byte for byte.
help_out_of_date.known_false_positives: None. The comparison is against the generator's own output.

help_topic_missing.title: A menu that opens the help at a topic which does not exist
help_topic_missing.why_it_matters: Opening the help at a renamed topic does not fail - it shows the FIRST topic instead, so the menu item appears to work and quietly answers a different question. This is the silent name mismatch that keeps costing this project time, in the one place where the reader has no way to tell they were sent somewhere else.
help_topic_missing.method: Every `startAt = "id"` and `openHelp("id", ...)` literal in app/qml, checked against the ids in config/help_topics.json. Section arguments are checked against that file's section ids the same way.
help_topic_missing.known_false_positives: A topic id built at run time rather than written as a literal; none exists, and one would not be checkable from here.

identical_branches.title: Both arms of a branch do the same thing
identical_branches.why_it_matters: Either the condition is pointless or one arm was meant to differ and does not - usually a copy-paste that was never finished.
identical_branches.method: An if/else whose two bodies have identical token sequences.

invokable_in_private_section.title: A Q_INVOKABLE QML can see and C++ hides
invokable_in_private_section.why_it_matters: Q_INVOKABLE in a private section is callable from QML and not from C++. It usually means the access specifier moved and the method did not.
invokable_in_private_section.method: Methods marked Q_INVOKABLE whose enclosing access section is private or protected.
invokable_in_private_section.known_false_positives: Deliberate: a method meant only for QML.

leftover_marker.title: A TODO, FIXME or HACK
leftover_marker.why_it_matters: A note somebody left for themselves and did not come back to.
leftover_marker.method: Comment tokens containing TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, BUG, WORKAROUND or TEMPORARY as whole words.
leftover_marker.known_false_positives: None - it is a literal search, reported for completeness.

mutable_static.title: Mutable state shared across every call
mutable_static.why_it_matters: A non-const static is shared by every caller and every thread. In a render path that is a data race waiting for a second thread.
mutable_static.method: Function-local and file-scope statics whose declaration has no const and no constexpr.
mutable_static.known_false_positives: Deliberate caches and singletons where the lock is not visible from the declaration. A static whose function or whose own type mentions a mutex, lock or atomic is NOT reported: the prompt was to check the locking, and if it is visibly there the prompt is noise. Nor is one whose immediately preceding comment is about threading - a declaration that has written down which thread touches it and when has answered the question this check asks, and reporting it anyway is how a low-severity check becomes wallpaper. `thread_local` is excluded too - it is per-thread, which is the opposite of shared.

notify_never_emitted.title: A Q_PROPERTY whose NOTIFY signal is never emitted
notify_never_emitted.why_it_matters: QML binds to a property through its NOTIFY signal. If nothing ever emits it, every binding on that property is evaluated once and then frozen - the UI simply stops updating, with no error anywhere.
notify_never_emitted.method: The NOTIFY signal named by each Q_PROPERTY, looked for as an EMISSION - `emit sig()`, `sig()`, `this->sig()` - anywhere in the C++ tree, rather than as a mention. See _emits below for why the distinction is the whole check.
notify_never_emitted.known_false_positives: Signals emitted through a macro or from generated code.

oversized_function.title: A function too large to hold in your head
oversized_function.why_it_matters: Length alone is weak evidence; length together with branching and nesting is the shape of a function that is hard to change without breaking something.
oversized_function.method: Functions over 220 lines, or with cyclomatic complexity over 60, or nested more than 6 deep. Reported with all three numbers so the reader can judge which is the problem.
oversized_function.known_false_positives: Dispatch tables and long switch statements are long but simple; their complexity number is high and their nesting is not. A function with complexity 3 or less and no nesting is a literal data table and is deliberately not reported however long it is. Nor is a DISPATCH CHAIN - a long run of independent branches that each answer and return - or a single expression built from a long chain of comparisons: see `_is_dispatch_chain` for why those two are the right shape rather than a problem.

py_bare_except.title: A bare `except:`
py_bare_except.why_it_matters: It catches KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit too, so it can swallow the user's attempt to stop the program.
py_bare_except.method: except handlers with no exception type.

py_dead_function.title: A module-level function nothing calls
py_dead_function.why_it_matters: Code nobody runs is code nobody is testing.
py_dead_function.method: Module-level functions whose name appears nowhere else in any Python file, are not dunders, do not start with an underscore, are not decorated, and are not test functions.
py_dead_function.known_false_positives: Functions called by name through getattr, or exported as an API. Names that appear in an import statement anywhere are counted as used.

py_except_pass.title: An except that swallows the error
py_except_pass.why_it_matters: The failure leaves no trace and the caller sees success.
py_except_pass.method: except handlers whose body is only `pass` or `...` AND carry no comment saying why. A handler that explains itself is doing the right thing and is not reported.
py_except_pass.known_false_positives: None known. A handler whose reason is given somewhere other than a comment in the handler itself.

py_flakes.title: A dead assignment, a dead import or an f-string with nothing in it
py_flakes.why_it_matters: The audit reads Python with its own parser, which knows the shapes it was taught and no others. pyflakes resolves names properly, and what it finds here is the residue a refactor leaves: a variable computed and never read, an import kept after its last use, an f-string whose placeholder was removed. None of those is a defect on its own - and all of them are where a real one hides. One of them was hiding a real one: an unused `from runtime import literature_dir` was the only thing making that function look alive, and it had had no caller for as long as it existed.
py_flakes.method: Runs pyflakes over services/python and tools, and reports two of its messages: an unused local, and an f-string with no placeholder. An unused import is left to `py_unused_import`, which already answers that.
py_flakes.known_false_positives: Two categories are dropped and both for a reason measured here. `redefinition of unused` fires on the service's operation dispatch, where each `if op==...` branch imports what that branch needs - mutually exclusive by construction and correct. And a line carrying `noqa` is skipped, because pyflakes does not honour it and this project uses it to record a deliberate import - `from uncertainties import umath` registers the maths functions and binds nothing.

py_mutable_default.title: A mutable default argument
py_mutable_default.why_it_matters: A default list or dict is created once, at definition time, and shared by every call. Appending to it in one call changes it for all the others - the classic Python trap, and silent.
py_mutable_default.method: Function parameters whose default is a list, dict or set literal, or a call to list(), dict() or set().

py_syntax_error.title: A Python file that does not parse
py_syntax_error.why_it_matters: It cannot run. If it is imported anywhere, that import fails.
py_syntax_error.known_false_positives: None - it is the compiler's own answer.

py_unused_import.title: An import nothing uses
py_unused_import.why_it_matters: Dead weight, and occasionally a rename left half-finished.
py_unused_import.method: Imported names that appear nowhere else in the module, excluding `__init__.py` re-exports and anything listed in `__all__`.
py_unused_import.known_false_positives: Imports purely for their side effects. A name used only inside a quoted type annotation is NOT reported: whole-word occurrences across the file are counted, not just AST references.

qml_anchors_conflict.title: An anchor and an explicit size on one item
qml_anchors_conflict.why_it_matters: Qt applies one and warns about the other, and which one wins depends on evaluation order. The layout looks right until something reorders.
qml_anchors_conflict.method: An object that sets `anchors.fill` and also width, height, x or y; or that sets `anchors.centerIn` and also x or y. centerIn does not size an item, so a width alongside it is required rather than conflicting.
qml_anchors_conflict.known_false_positives: Setting width alongside anchors.fill is legal when the anchor is conditional, which this does not model.

qml_binding_overwritten.title: A property with both a binding and an imperative assignment
qml_binding_overwritten.why_it_matters: Assigning to a property in JavaScript destroys its binding permanently. The property stops tracking whatever it was following, and nothing says so - it simply stops updating.
qml_binding_overwritten.method: A property that has a declarative binding ON THE SAME OBJECT and is also the target of a plain `=` assignment inside that object's own handlers or functions. Assignments of `Qt.binding(...)` are excluded: that is the documented way to put a binding BACK, so reporting it says the opposite of what the code does.
qml_binding_overwritten.known_false_positives: Assignments guarded so they only run once, and properties whose binding is deliberately temporary. A property initialised to a literal constant is not treated as bound, because there is nothing for the assignment to destroy.

qml_bool_from_and.title: A bool property bound to `a && b`
qml_bool_from_and.why_it_matters: In JavaScript `a && b` evaluates to A when A is falsy, so when A is undefined the binding yields undefined rather than false. Qt refuses to assign that to a bool and leaves the property at its DEFAULT - which means the value is the same whether the code is correct or broken, and only the runtime warning tells them apart. This project shipped fourteen instances of it.
qml_bool_from_and.method: A property declared `bool` whose binding is a top-level `&&` or `||` chain with an operand that is an OBJECT reference rather than a boolean: not a comparison, not a negation, not a literal, and not ending in a name declared `bool` anywhere in QML or in a Q_PROPERTY. That last test is the discriminator - `canvas && canvas.parametric` is the bug, `root.hasData && !root.app.busy` is not, and only the declared type of the final component tells them apart.
qml_bool_from_and.known_false_positives:
An operand that is genuinely always defined but whose type this cannot see - a property supplied by a parent component, for instance.
Deliberately NOT reported: `a && b ? x : y`, where the && is the ternary's condition and is coerced to boolean before anything is assigned.

qml_build_list_mismatch.title: A QML file the build list and the disk disagree about
qml_build_list_mismatch.why_it_matters: A file on disk but not in GRAPHVIS_QML_FILES cannot be imported at runtime; a file in the list but not on disk fails the build. Both are silent until the moment they are not.
qml_build_list_mismatch.method: The set difference, both ways, between GRAPHVIS_QML_FILES in app/CMakeLists.txt and the .qml files under app/qml - except that a file named ANYWHERE in CMakeLists is treated as accounted for, since a lazily-loaded view is legitimately added as a raw resource instead.
qml_build_list_mismatch.known_false_positives: A file mentioned in CMakeLists only in a comment.

qml_completed_in_delegate.title: Component.onCompleted inside a repeated delegate
qml_completed_in_delegate.why_it_matters: A delegate is created and destroyed as the view scrolls, so anything onCompleted does - registering, reparenting, appending to a model - happens again on every recycle and never gets undone. This project has already had one reparenting bug of exactly this shape.
qml_completed_in_delegate.method: A non-empty `Component.onCompleted` handler on an object inside a delegate, contentItem, highlight or other per-item property of a view or repeater.
qml_completed_in_delegate.known_false_positives: Delegates in a view that is never scrolled or rebuilt.

qml_cpp_member_missing.title: QML reads a member off a C++ object that the C++ class does not have
qml_cpp_member_missing.why_it_matters: The controller, the canvas and the project workspace all arrive in QML as `property var`, so nothing static can see what they are: qmllint resolves them to nothing and checks nothing, and the application has 322 reads across that boundary. A rename on either side is silent - the read yields undefined, the binding quietly does nothing, and the control behind it stops working with no message. `openExport` shipped in that state and File > Export did nothing at all.
qml_cpp_member_missing.method: Collects every `app.x`, `canvas.x` and `project.x` in the QML and compares them against the Q_PROPERTY, Q_INVOKABLE and signal names declared in that object's own header. QQuickItem's own members are excluded for the canvas, which is one.
qml_cpp_member_missing.known_false_positives: A local JavaScript variable named `app`, `canvas` or `project` would be read as the object. There are none. A member reached through a chain - `app.project.name` - is checked at each named prefix and not beyond.

qml_delegate_missing_required_model.title: A delegate that declares a required property and still uses `model`
qml_delegate_missing_required_model.why_it_matters: Qt 6 stops injecting the implicit `model`, `index` and `modelData` into a delegate as soon as that delegate declares any `required property`. Code that used them keeps compiling and fails at runtime with 'ReferenceError: model is not defined'. This project shipped that bug.
qml_delegate_missing_required_model.method: A delegate object declaring at least one `required property`, which references `model`, `index` or `modelData` without declaring those as required properties itself.
qml_delegate_missing_required_model.known_false_positives: None known. An earlier version of this check looked sixty lines past a Repeater for the two texts and matched 72 unrelated sites; it was deleted. This one asks the object tree which properties the delegate declares, which is the question that was always being asked.

qml_signal_never_handled.title: A signal nothing connects to
qml_signal_never_handled.why_it_matters: A signal declared and never handled is either dead, or the handler was renamed and the signal was not.
qml_signal_never_handled.method: A declared signal whose `onName` handler appears in no QML file and whose name appears in no C++ source.
qml_signal_never_handled.known_false_positives: Signals handled by a name built at runtime, or connected from C++ with a string.

qml_type_error.title: QML that names a property or method its type does not have
qml_type_error.why_it_matters: A QML file that reads a member the type does not have is not a compile error and not a runtime error either - the read yields undefined, the binding quietly does nothing, and the button it was behind stops working with no message anywhere. Two of those shipped: a notebook delegate that re-declared a property its base type already had, so every figure in the notebook reported itself as figure zero and the close button removed the wrong one; and an `openExport` declared four levels deep instead of on the workspace root, which left File > Export doing nothing at all.
qml_type_error.method: Runs Qt's own qmllint against the application's QML, staged as a module through the SAME function the interface tests use - so the C++ types have their generated stand-ins and the linter can resolve them. Two message shapes are reported and the rest are dropped: a property that already exists in the base type, and a member not found on a NAMED type.
qml_type_error.known_false_positives: A member read off a Loader's `item` is reported by qmllint against type QObject, because that is what `item` is to a static reader, and there are sixteen of those here that are all correct code. They are dropped by name: a finding against QObject is not reported. That exclusion is why the seventeenth - the real one, against VisualizeWorkspace - was worth reporting rather than lost in the noise.

qml_unresolved_id.title: A reference to an id that does not exist
qml_unresolved_id.why_it_matters: An unresolvable id is a runtime ReferenceError that Qt reports once per evaluation, and a binding that silently never produces a value.
qml_unresolved_id.method: A lowercase identifier used at the head of a member expression inside a binding, which is not: an id declared in this file, a property or function in scope, a JavaScript local, a known global, a QML built-in, or a C++ context property. Anything the model cannot see is treated as resolvable, so this errs heavily towards silence.
qml_unresolved_id.known_false_positives: Ids injected by a parent component, and roles supplied by a model - both of which are why the earlier regex version produced 1,033 false positives and had to be deleted.

qml_unused_property.title: A declared property nothing reads
qml_unused_property.why_it_matters: A property declared and never read is either dead weight or a rename that was only half done - the old name still declared, the new one used.
qml_unused_property.method: A property declared on an object whose name appears nowhere else in any QML file and in no C++ source, and which is not an override of a known Qt property.
qml_unused_property.known_false_positives: Properties read only from C++ through a name built at runtime, and properties that exist to be set by a parent component. A read-only property is exempt when the object declares three or more of that type: that is an enumeration or a scale spelled out, and half an enumeration is worse than an unused one.

repeated_subcondition.title: The same test twice in one condition
repeated_subcondition.why_it_matters: `a && a` and `a || a` are always a typo for a second, different test.
repeated_subcondition.method: Identical operands either side of && or || within one condition, compared as token sequences at the top level of the expression.

self_comparison.title: An expression compared with itself
self_comparison.why_it_matters: `a == a` and `a - a` are constants. Either a typo for a nearby name or left over from an edit.
self_comparison.method: Identical token sequences either side of <, >, <= or >= within one statement. Equality is deliberately excluded: `x == x` and `x != x` are the standard idiom for testing whether a float is NaN, and reporting them produced 14 findings here, all of them that idiom.
self_comparison.known_false_positives: None known, now that equality is excluded.

shadowed_declaration.title: An inner name hiding an outer one
shadowed_declaration.why_it_matters: Two different variables with one name in overlapping scopes. The reader has to track which is which, and an edit in the wrong place compiles.
shadowed_declaration.method: A declaration in a nested scope with the same name as one in an enclosing scope of the same function.
shadowed_declaration.known_false_positives: Deliberate shadowing in short lambdas, which is idiomatic.

swallowed_exception.title: A catch that does nothing
swallowed_exception.why_it_matters: An empty catch turns a failure into a wrong answer with no trace. The program carries on as if the work succeeded.
swallowed_exception.method: A catch clause whose body contains no statements, or only a comment.
swallowed_exception.known_false_positives: Catches that are deliberately empty because the failure is genuinely expected - these should say so in a comment, which this does not currently read.

switch_fallthrough.title: A switch arm that falls into the next
switch_fallthrough.why_it_matters: Almost always a missing break. When deliberate it is conventionally marked, so an unmarked fallthrough with real work in it is a good bet.
switch_fallthrough.method: A `case` label whose statements neither terminate nor are empty, followed by another `case`, with no fallthrough comment or attribute on the intervening lines.
switch_fallthrough.known_false_positives: Deliberate fallthrough marked in a way this does not recognise.

theme_cvd_tags_stale.title: A theme whose colour-vision tag no longer matches its colours
theme_cvd_tags_stale.why_it_matters: The tags decide which themes the picker offers once a colour-vision mode is set. A theme whose colours were edited without re-measuring keeps its old verdict, so it is either offered to a reader it no longer serves or hidden from one it does - and both are invisible from the file.
theme_cvd_tags_stale.method: Runs tools/measure_theme_cvd.py --check, which re-simulates every theme's positive/warning/danger colours through each deficiency and compares the verdict against the `safe` field on that theme's own line.
theme_cvd_tags_stale.known_false_positives: None. It is the same tool that writes the tags.

theme_name_missing.title: A Theme property that does not exist
theme_name_missing.why_it_matters: QML resolves names at runtime, so a size bound to a Theme property nobody declared is not an error: the text simply comes out at the default and nobody notices. `Theme.fontSizeLarge` shipped that way.
theme_name_missing.method: Every `Theme.<name>` reference in any QML file, checked against the properties, functions and enum values actually declared in Theme.qml.
theme_name_missing.known_false_positives: Properties added to Theme from C++ at runtime.

two_answers.title: Two independent answers to one question
two_answers.why_it_matters: When one property is computed in two places, the two drift apart and the program believes both. This project has hit it repeatedly - most recently a window title reading one notion of the project name while the project itself held another.
two_answers.method: Within one class, parameterless const methods with the same return type that read exactly the same set of member fields but have different bodies.
two_answers.known_false_positives: Deliberate pairs - a value and its formatted form, a getter and a cached variant - legitimately share inputs.

unreachable_code.title: A statement control can never arrive at
unreachable_code.why_it_matters: Code after an unconditional return, break, continue or throw never runs. If it looks important, something is wrong above it.
unreachable_code.method: Statements following a statement from which control cannot fall through, within the same block. Labels clear the state, so switch arms are not reported, and a preprocessor conditional between the two suppresses the finding because only one arm compiles.

unused_local.title: A local that is never read
unused_local.why_it_matters: Dead weight, and sometimes a symptom: a value computed and then not used is often a line that was meant to be used and is not.
unused_local.method: A declared local with no reads, no writes and no address taken, whose type is primitive - so construction and destruction cannot have effects - and whose name is not declared more than once in the function.
unused_local.known_false_positives: None known: class-typed locals (RAII guards) and names declared in several #ifdef arms are deliberately excluded.

vision_mode_list_mismatch.title: Theme.qml names a different number of colour-vision modes from C++
vision_mode_list_mismatch.why_it_matters: Theme.visionKinds is indexed by the program's colour-vision mode number. A mode added to colourVisionNames() and not here reads as no mode at all, so the theme filter silently stops applying for it - and a mode removed leaves every later index pointing at the wrong deficiency, which filters against the wrong measurement.
vision_mode_list_mismatch.method: Counts the QStringLiteral entries in colourVisionNames() in ColourVision.h and the entries in Theme.qml's visionKinds, and compares.
vision_mode_list_mismatch.known_false_positives: None. They are one list written twice, which is why this exists.
